Subject: GPU runway clearance request — Opsync Labs (OPS-8421)

Team,

Opsync (contact: Maya Patel) signaled a late-stage commercial commitment this morning — they want production-grade dedicated capacity to meet a Sept launch. I need a quick clearance on available GPU runway and a tentative allocation plan we can present to their procurement team by EOD tomorrow. Key asks: 

- Short checklist: confirm available SKUs and counts across US zones (A100-80GB, H100, L4) for the period 2026-09-01 through 2026-12-31.
- Recommended warm pool sizing: they expect an initial ramp of ~20 concurrent GPUs with burst to ~120 for peak. Suggest minimum reserved commit and an overflow policy.
- Potential conflicts: list any other committed deals in the same timeframe that would block fulfillment.
- Fallback options: viable model/quantization combos if H100s are constrained (e.g., A100 quantized, L4 for rep scoring).

I attached the current capacity snapshot and a draft runway plan to orient the discussion. Please reply with availability and one recommended allocation (minimal, target, fallback) so I can loop opsync procurement and share a short mutual action plan.

Attachments: [Attachment: capacity_snapshot_20260615.csv (csv)], [Attachment: deal_runway_plan_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Sales

Sergio —

Quick availability readout after checking cluster reservations and upcoming capacity maintenance windows: 

- US-west-1: H100 (80GB) available: 40 nodes free for Sept; A100-80GB available: 22 nodes; L4 available: 120 nodes.
- US-east-1: H100 available: 12 nodes; A100: 30 nodes; L4: 95 nodes.

Constraints: we have two near-term commitments (internal deal tags: TRN-610, QNT-999) that overlap a portion of Sept and reduce H100 headroom by ~18 nodes if both fully ramp. Maintenance window in us-west-1 planned 2026-09-14 — we can shift workloads or use cross-region routing for that week.

My recommended allocation for Opsync: 
- Minimal: reserve 20 L4 nodes + 8 A100 nodes (covers eval + low latency dev).
- Target: reserve 20 H100 nodes + 40 A100 nodes + 20 L4 warm pool (handles initial ramp to ~100 concurrent tokens/sec).
- Fallback: if H100s drop below 16 nodes, use A100 quantized + KV cache tuning; can hit 0.9x latency with modest quality tradeoff.

I attached node mapping notes and a short checklist for rollout impact. A few operational asks: we should hold a tentative window (72 hrs) to let sales finalize legal/term questions — otherwise nodes may be reallocated.

Attachments: [Attachment: node_mapping_notes.txt (txt)]

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Dedicated Capacity Planning

Sergio/Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turn. Sales position: Opsync has signaled an intent to commit pending standard procurement and an SLA note. I approve a 72-hour tentative block (internal term: runway-lock) on the target allocation Karthik recommended, subject to: 

1) Opsync sends a signed PO or an executed MSA within 72 hours.
2) Scoped SLA document agreed (I attached the SLA matrix we typically use for Dedicated pilots).
3) We do not reallocate resources already under active paid commitment.

Camila/Vivek — please treat this as a priority; if allocation would risk an existing paid commitment, escalate to me immediately. Sergio — when you loop procurement, make it explicit this is a tentative block and not a guaranteed reservation until the PO/MSA is in hand.

Attachments: [Attachment: sla_matrix.pdf (pdf)]

—Lauren
